producer_report.summary: When a job's request names commit hashes (7 to 40 hex characters with a digit and a letter, at most 8), the producer and verifier snapshots now get one read-only text file, `ATHENA-COMMITS.txt`. For each named commit in the base's history it holds the full hash, date, subject, visible paths and their diff. The core builds it from the user's repository with the same `classify()` filter as `HISTORY.txt`. `records/`, `athena-exclude` paths, submodule entries, commit bodies and authors are never written. No object, ref, alternate or remote enters the snapshot, and the file is listed in the snapshot's `.git/info/exclude`, so it never reaches a candidate, change list or prepared tree. Unknown or non-commit hashes, commits outside the base's history and hidden-only commits get one shared note; the job is not refused. The brief gains a sentence naming the file only when the request names a hash, so no-hash briefs and snapshots are unchanged. The sentence says to read the file by its path, because a directory-wide Grep skips excluded files. In athena-git: `Snapshot::add_commit_views`, `CommitViews`, `COMMITS_FILE`, `Git::diff_text` and `Git::date_and_subject`. In athena-context: `commit_hashes_in` and `COMMITS_FILE`. In athena-core: `verifier_snapshot_for` is used at the three agent-read call sites, and the 4-argument `verifier_snapshot` stays as a wrapper for the scratch snapshot in checks.rs. docs/decisions.md could not be edited in place because it is append-only, so I added D155. I added row M34 to docs/enforcement.md and a CHANGELOG entry. fmt, clippy, the full test suite and the policy scan all pass.

criteria_check.criterion: A new athena-git test builds a user repo with an extra commit, creates a producer snapshot with that commit requested, and checks the commit's visible changes (subject, paths, diff) are readable inside the snapshot. Run `cargo test -p athena-git`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `named_commit_is_readable_in_a_producer_snapshot` in crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs builds a user repo plus an extra commit and a later one, creates a SnapshotRepo::Base snapshot, calls add_commit_views, and asserts the file holds the full hash, `subject Add the feature`, paths src/feature.rs and src/main.rs, `+++ b/src/feature.rs`, the added line, the removed line and a 10-character date. A second case uses a 7-character abbreviation of an ancestor. `cargo test -p athena-git` passed (66 tests).

criteria_check.criterion: A test commits a change to an athena-exclude path and to records/ in a requested commit. It checks that neither the content nor the path name appears anywhere in the snapshot, including the history view. Run `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `hidden_paths_never_appear_in_the_commit_view`: the requested commit changes src/main.rs plus FRONT.md, private/notes.md and records/jobs/y.json, each with a marker. It builds Base and BaseAndCandidate snapshots, then checks every file name and byte under the snapshot dir including .git, plus `git log --all -p` and `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch`. No marker or hidden path name is found. FRONT.md and the words records/private are asserted absent from ATHENA-COMMITS.txt only, because the visible root .gitattributes names FRONT.md. A PlainWithHistory HISTORY.txt is checked too. A control runs unfiltered `git show` on the same commits and finds all markers and names, so the assertions can fail. A hidden-only commit is omitted and its subject is absent. Passed in `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -q`.

criteria_check.criterion: A test checks that the snapshot has no path back to the user's repository (no alternates, no remotes) and that the user's refs and objects are unchanged after creation. Run `cargo test`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `commit_view_gives_the_snapshot_no_path_to_the_users_repository`: no objects/info/alternates or http-alternates, `git remote` empty, config without url or alternate, no file under the snapshot holds the user's directory path, the snapshot's git cannot resolve the real commit hashes, and it has one commit. The user's for-each-ref, cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch-check output, HEAD and .git/config are identical before and after. Passed in the full run.

My first athena-git tests had a clippy cloned_ref_to_slice_refs violation and one wrong expectation (a kept-directory seed deletes the base's other files, so the change list is not just the added file). Both fixed.
The first draft of the view header named `records/` and private paths, which would put a hidden path name into the snapshot; reworded before any test run.
learnings: docs/decisions.md is append-only: athena-cli's `the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to` pins the first 230046 bytes, so a decision cannot be reworded. A new entry must be appended, with a Provenance bullet and ids ascending.

The decision-link backtest parses the phrases 'superseded by', 'supersedes' and 'amends' against docs/decision-links.toml; a new entry that uses them without a confirmed link is a finding. D155 avoids them.
`git diff` does not accept --pathspec-from-file, so Git::diff_text passes literal paths in chunks of 100 after `--` with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1.
Test `Tweak` closures in run_pin_tests.rs run while the agent's snapshot still exists, so they can inspect the workdir and its git status; the directory is removed after the job.
docs/enforcement.md rows are checked by an xtask test that every backticked test name exists, so a new row must name only real tests.
